Now he lived seventy years,
and he reigned thirty years;
out of these, he ruled over Baghdad for eight years.
And that Sultan had commanded
that Sulayman, the son of Chaghrï Beg, should sit upon his throne.
However, Alp Arslan, his brother,
because he was powerful,
deposed him,
and he himself reigned.
And he was proclaimed in Baghdad and in all the lands as Sultan Diya al-Din.
And in the year 1376 [of the Greeks],
[that is] 456 of the Arabs, certain Kurdish hunters spread a report in Baghdad,
saying, "While we were hunting in the desert,
we saw black curtains, and the sound of dancing, weeping, and great wailing.
And when we drew near, we heard a voice saying:
'Today Beelzebub, the chief of the demons, has died.
And any place where a house of weeping is not made for him for three days,
we will uproot it from its foundations.'"
And when the women of Baghdad heard this folly,
they went out to the cemetery,
and they sat for three days, wailing and weeping, and tearing their garments,
and plucking out their hair,
and blackening their faces with the soot of pots,
so that, as they said, by this they might appease the demons,
and that they would not kill their loved ones.
And this report spread throughout the whole land of Shinar,
and in every place it was done just as in Baghdad,
namely in Mosul and in Armenia.
And in this year, Sultan Alp Arslan went against the city of Ani,
which was the foremost city of the Romans in the region of the Armenia of the Armenians,
and he conquered it,
and made a great slaughter in it.
For concerning the strength of Ani it is related
that on three of its sides the great river Aras surrounds it,
and on the other side a deep moat is dug,
into which also much water from the Aras passes with great force.
And the inhabitants of the city enter and go out over a bridge.
For there were in it seven hundred thousand courtyards and a thousand churches.
And when the Turks had given up hope of taking it,
suddenly, by a divine sign, one of its towers fell,
and they placed a bridge and entered it.
And from this, that Sultan was called Abu'l-Fath.
And in the first Tishrin of this year,
there was intense heat in Baghdad until the first Kanun.
And sickness and pestilence followed it,
so that a mana of tamarind was sold for four (four hundred?) gold dinars.
